item.research_question: How can the low fracture toughness of superhard high-entropy carbides (HECs) be enhanced while maintaining high hardness?
item.material_system: (W0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Zr0.2Ti0.2)C high-entropy carbide with in-situ tetragonal and monoclinic ZrO2 particles
item.processing_route: Powder metallurgy: equimolar mixing of WC, TaC, NbC, ZrC, TiC powders; ball milling at 250 rpm for 110 h; Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at 1800 °C for 5 min under 30 MPa or 50 MPa uniaxial pressure
item.test_conditions: Room temperature compression testing; Vickers hardness testing at 9.8, 49, and 294 N loads; Fracture toughness measured via Single Edge Notched Beam (SENB, ASTM C 1421-18) and indentation methods
key_findings: The HEC sintered at 50 MPa achieved a Vickers hardness of 21.0 GPa (at 9.8 N load).
The fracture toughness (KIC) of the HEC sintered at 50 MPa reached 5.89 ± 0.19 MPa·m1/2 via the SENB method.
The fracture toughness value was 73% higher than that estimated from the rule of mixture (ROM).
Higher sintering pressure (50 MPa) increased the fraction of retained metastable tetragonal ZrO2 to ~85.3% in the as-sintered state.
Upon fracturing, ~18.5% of the tetragonal ZrO2 particles transformed into monoclinic ZrO2.
Transformation toughening contributed 1.0 MPa·m1/2 to the total fracture toughness.
Crack bridging contributed 0.41 MPa·m1/2, while microcrack toughening contributed 0.16 MPa·m1/2 (dilatational) and 0.23 MPa·m1/2 (modulus).
The average grain size of the FCC matrix decreased from 2.3 μm (30 MPa) to ~1.5 μm (50 MPa).
item.mechanism: The toughening is primarily attributed to the stress-induced martensitic transformation of metastable tetragonal ZrO2 particles to monoclinic ZrO2 under mechanical loading, which generates a transformation-induced wake zone that shields the crack tip. This is supplemented by crack deflection, crack bridging, and microcrack branching caused by thermal expansion mismatch and residual stresses around the ZrO2 particles.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The authors propose that fracture toughness can be further enhanced by optimizing the design and processing, such as adjusting the relative fraction of Zr in non-equimolar variants, amending the oxygen partial pressure in the sintering chamber, and refining the ZrO2 particles in the HEC matrix.
quotes: Here, we introduce a metastability engineering strategy to achieve superhard HECs with enhanced toughness via in-situ metastable particles.

The toughening effect is primarily attributed to the transformation of the metastable tetragonal ZrO2 particles under mechanical loading, which promotes crack tip shielding mechanisms including crack deflection, crack bridging and crack branching.
The work demonstrates the concept of using in-situ metastable particles for toughening bulk high-entropy ceramics by taking advantage of their compositional flexibility.
